walkthroughs.body_html:
Water & Aquatic Food Systems — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Water & Aquatic Food Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Water & Aquatic Food Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Schaefer's maximum sustainable yield model dates from:
Newfoundland cod fishery moratorium was imposed in:
How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Fertiliser directly poisons fish.
Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.

mcqs.q: What is the leading driver of global deforestation?
options: Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Logging for timber and paper.
Agriculture (especially cattle ranching, soy, palm oil).
Forest fires alone.
Acid rain falling on the ocean.
Dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid, lowering ocean pH.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
